utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: As for the next witness, I am afraid I have not been given, as requested, any indication of who is calling the witness. Yes, Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I didn't have the transcript yesterday afternoon so I made the list only for the following week, so I would just like to tell you that we've changed the schedule of witnesses. Mr. Vlado Divkovic will testify first because he has to leave today, and Mr. Rudo Kurevija will be examined later. I will be examining Mr. Divkovic, and my colleague, Mr. Radovic, will be questioning Mr. Rudo Kurevija after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Formally speaking who has called Mr. Divkovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Formally speaking, Mr. Radovic and myself called these witnesses. He is not on the prior list, but you decided on January 11th of '99 at a session, which was later -- which we received in writing, that we can question Mr. Divkovic without further formalities. He wasn't on the original list because the person who was originally supposed to testify to these circumstances could not appear, so we had to invite a new person, and this was approved by the Trial Chamber. So we are calling him on behalf of the Defence of Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: No. So that means that the next witness will be examined in chief by yourself and by Counsel Radovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: And will be cross-examined by the other Defence counsel. All right. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Divkovic. Could you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Examined by Ms. Slokovic-Glumac:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Divkovic.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us for the record when and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I was born in Varos, Bosnia and Herzegovina, on the 16th of March, 1948.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your occupation is?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm an economist. I have a degree in economics at the University of Rijeka in the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what you were doing in '91, '92, and '93? What was your job at that time?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I have been working and living in Vitez since 1980. Since 1980 until 1987, I was working as a director of a part of the Vitezit company, and then from '87 to '93, I was the general manager of the Vitezit company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Vitezit factory, together with other factories such as SPS and Sintevit, was a part of the military industry facilities in Vitez; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the factory Slobodan Princip Seljo and Sintevit were part of the Yugoslav military industry which were located in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what was their main product?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The production of rocket fuels and gunpowder was manufactured by the SPS factory, and Sintevit produced explosives and PVC granulates as well as PVC packaging.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said about Vitezit --

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, industrial explosives and gunpowder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these factories linked together?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The complete chain of the military industry in the former Yugoslavia was linked. They never produced products individually or made final products, because each of them made components which were then put together. So they were technologically dependent on one another. They were linked. We're talking about military production.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please wait for me to complete the question, because we're overlapping. So were these three factories linked by some common facilities, some management bodies, did they act jointly? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were technologically linked as well as managerially. One factory was producing products which were used by the other two, and this was the case for the other factories, so one could not really operate without the others. Therefore, it's logical that the management bodies were also coordinating the production process between the three factories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Vitez itself, what was the significance of these three factories? What was their importance?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, their importance was in the fact that they employed 2.400 workers. Maybe that would be more than 50 per cent of the overall work-force in Vitez. The factories were oriented to the Yugoslav export market, and they had a considerable profit and they provided a livelihood for a lot of the population in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that 2.400 people were employed there. Does that mean that almost half of the working population of Vitez was in some way involved in the production?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. More than 50 per cent of the work-force in Vitez worked in these three factories.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what was the effect of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina to the factory? What did it mean?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when I said that the military industry of the former Yugoslavia were all linked, of course as a result of the Serb aggression against Bosnia and Herzegovina the effect of that was great. At the beginning of the war we did not get our regular supplies from East Serbia and Eastern Bosnia, and we also lost our buyers on the market, and we lost the market where 30 or 40 per cent of our production was sold. So at the beginning the war the possibility -- the capacities of the factory were reduced by 50 per cent and thereby also our ability to employ new workers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the employees were Serbs, Muslims and Croats in these factories?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were Serbs, Muslims and Croats at the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a mistranslation. Are you talking about the beginning of the aggression?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking about the start of the Serb aggression against Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, in September of '92, these factories were bombarded by the Serbs, or by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on September 19th the factories were bombarded and the vital facilities were destroyed at that time, even further reducing our production capacity, so that in the coming period after the 19th of September we only were operating at 30 to 40 per cent capacity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what were the consequences of such a situation, war on one side and then bombardment and destruction of facilities?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The consequences were our reduction of capacity, inability to employ more employees, then also laying off the employees and then, of course, a major cut in salaries and problems in making a living.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When workers were laid off, who were the people who were being laid off?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I stated that we were using 30 to 40 per cent of our capacity, so that a large number of our workers were laid off. This was carried out on a rotation basis so that every month a new group of employees were laid off. The lists of the people to be laid off were determined at the management -- at a higher level of management. So the basic principle was to rotate the employees so that they would all go through a period of being laid off. Their salaries were cut, but in view of the fact that at that time we had problems to supply our workers with basic consumer goods, basic foods, a part of the salaries was distributed in food, and everybody received food regardless of the fact they were laid off or not. So the fact that they were laid off really didn't have much effect on their earnings at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the people who were laid off did receive a part of their salary as well as assistance in food, the same as those who were working?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The workers who were laid off received 70 per cent of their salary in cash, and then also received the rest in food, just like all the other workers who were not laid off at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the salaries like?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: At that time our salaries were low. The average salary was between 40 and 50 German Marks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is this period that we're talking about?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a period from the second half of '92 until April '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there -- was there any discrimination in determining who would be laid off?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In order for me to respond to this question I would have to give a little bit of the background regarding the personnel structure. No national or ethic identity in this matter. We didn't really deal with that. We were primarily thinking about technology, and we wanted to rotate all the people who were being laid off. So there was no national factor in this. I will explain later that even if we wanted to do this, we could not do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was no discrimination?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: No, none whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The number of employees in the factory was about 2.400 you said. What was the structure?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The structure --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please wait a little bit? Okay. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The national structure of the employed was similar to the structure of the population in Vitez. So 46 per cent Croats, 42 per cent Muslims, and about 6 to 7 per cent of Serbs, and then the rest were others and those who declared themselves as Yugoslavs, so about 6 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So basically they were equally represented, all the three ethnic groups were represented equally in the factories?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in the factory during the old order, attention was -- much attention was devoted to the national structure of the employees, so we tried to have the national structure of the employees reflect the national structure of the municipality. So this is how things were at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then this structure remained until the end?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the people employed reflected the composition of the population in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the managerial staff? How were they composed in ethnic terms in all three factories?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The situation was as follows, I'm talking about the first, second and third level: First, the general manager and his deputies, then the second level --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, Mr. Divkovic. Could we give the witness these lists?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is marked D53/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a review of the management personnel in the SPS of Vitez and in Sintevit Vitez. Could you tell us who compiled these lists?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: It says here for the SPS company it was drafted by Franjo Grabovac, deputy general manager. For the DP Sintevit, Dubravka Pavlovic, an employee in the personnel service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look through those lists for a moment?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm familiar with these lists, only there are some changes in the case of the Sintevit enterprise, because I checked some of the data and some of those listed here are not correct. If necessary, I can correct them. I can tell you the errors that have been made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: For example, the chief of production, where it says Ajsa Mujcic, production manager, Mr. Anto Pavlovic was performing those duties. Then also it says production manager Fehim Cepalo, it should be Niko Bobas. And the financial manager and chief accountant, instead of Faruk Licnia and Fahra Sivro, it was Zdravka Pranjkovic who performed both those duties together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from those corrections that you have made, having looked through the appropriate documents --

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: There should also be a list for the Vitezit enterprise, which has not been provided. As for these two social enterprises, the personnel composition was as follows: In the social enterprise, Slobodan Princip Zeljo or the SPS, out of total of 27 managerial staff, 13 were Croats or 48.1 per cent, there were 11 Muslims or 40.8 per cent, and 3 Serbs or 11.1 per cent. In the social enterprise Sintevit, out of total of 12 managerial staff, there were 3 Croats or 25 per cent, 9 Muslims or 75 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which means that 75 per cent of the managers were Muslims in the Sintevit enterprise, and 25 per cent of the managers were Croats. Was this the situation as it was on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These lists apply for the 15th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the verifications and corrections that you made?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We wanted to be sure that the lists were accurate as on the day of the 15th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, in the Vitezit enterprise of which you were the manager, can you tell us how the personnel were composed? I saw your tables and they are many, so to avoid photocopying can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In the Vitezit social enterprise, out of the total of 37 managers, 12 were Croats or 32.5 per cent, there were 20 Muslims or 54 per cent, 4 Serbs or 10.8 per cent, and one belonging to other ethnic groups or 2.7 per cent. If you wish me to add all this up for the whole area --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Tell us how many people were employed in Vitezit itself.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: About 1.070 workers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in SPS?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Nine hundred and sixty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in Sintevit?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The rest, which means about 300 and something, 370.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the level of these three enterprises, give us the figures for the managers overall.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: At the level of the whole enterprise, there were a total of 76 managerial posts. Twenty-eight of them were held by Croats or 36.9 per cent, 40 by Muslims or 52.6 per cent, 7 by Serbs or 9.2 per cent, and one belonged to other ethnic groups or 1.3 per cent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was it that in one of the enterprises, that is in Sintevit, almost the entire managerial staff were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I never thought about it until I had these names in front of me. All I can say is that the general manager of that enterprise was a Muslim, so if we can infer anything from that that could be the reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the situation as it was in Vitez and in Central Bosnia as a whole at the time, what were the relationships within the enterprises among the managers belonging to different ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I can tell you that the management that was there on the 15th of April, 1993 continued working with very few changes -- had been working with very few changes for the past six years. So that our relationship was very good amongst us in terms of management, and also personal relations amongst us were very good, without any divisions or misunderstandings on ethnic or any other grounds. Our main concerns were our business, our economy, and we harnessed all our efforts towards providing our workers with means of livelihood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of '92 or '93, were there cases of workers being fired or dismissed; do you recall any?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the enterprises in which I was the general manager?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Six workers were dismissed in '87 because they refused obedience. From then until '93, no one was dismissed, and as far as I know, there were no dismissals in the other two companies either, so that there were no workers fired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any problems with Muslim workers? Did they have to sign any kind of documents of allegiance to the enterprise or to the HVO? Have you ever heard about any such requirements?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: No, there were no such requirements or blackmail used among the workers. I must say that we successfully resisted the influence of all policies, because we clearly said, after the elections in 1991, politics should be left outside, outside the factory halls. Whatever you agree on, let us know. If it is something you have agreed upon, we will act accordingly. And that is how it functioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were never any instructions or directives from the civilian or the military HVO authorities to treat differently the Muslims in the factory or to show any kind of discrimination towards them?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: No, there was never any directive of that kind nor was there any discrimination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any attempts to replace the managers, particularly in this third factory which was virtually managed by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of that. You mean Sintevit?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any replacements that you do know of?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I know that I or, rather, my enterprise received a document in those days from the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Could I ask the usher for his assistance, to show this document to the witness and to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D54/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document, because you gave it to me anyway?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. This is a decision on the appointment of the temporary managing board and temporary management in the public corporation Vitezit. It is dated -- I can't remember -- November 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, you were the manager at the time, were you not?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was the manager of Vitezit, and Vitezit was a social, not a public, enterprise. However, at some kind of a meeting of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which could not function in those days as a government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, but it is well-known that the Serbs had walked out of that government at the beginning of '92, it is also known that Croats, because of the seizure of Sarajevo, could not physically attend the meeting, so that government met in such a way that only Muslims were present, and then they decided to appoint Nusret Kalco and move me to a member of the management board, and this was really an attempt to replace the general manager without any legality, and Nusret Kalco, who is a good friend of mine to this day, when he received this decision, he came up to me and said, "What is this, Manager?" And I said, "Well, if you don't know, I don't know certainly." And he said, "I have no idea." And he said, "Neither can I do this nor do I want to do it." So this decision was not implemented. It is noteworthy, something that we mentioned a moment ago, it may be the cause that prompted the writing of this decision, after the shelling of the factories by the Yugoslav People's Army, we received some kind of oral orders to prohibit all Serbs from entering the factory, the Serbs who had been working in the factory. We did not implement this order because we felt, and I am of the same opinion to this day, that the people cannot be held responsible for something the extremist members have done or are doing. So that those Serbs continued working until the end of '93. So it says here, Immediately rally and employ all the workers -- in one of these paragraphs it says, "Immediately rally and engage all workers who have not sided with the aggressor against Bosnia and Herzegovina, immediately terminate employment of all workers who have in any way sided with the aggressor."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who signed this decision?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: It was signed by the Vice-President of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Hakija Jurajlic, even though the Prime Minister was Jure Pelivan, who in talking to him, we learned from him, had never heard of this decision nor had he ever seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person who was supposed to succeed you, Nusret Kalco, he is a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is a Muslim, and he was my deputy, deputy director for production.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you said that he too was against such a decision?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: He was surprised by it, and he knew that there was no purpose in implementing it and he refused to do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that in '92, there were problems with the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, since, in your opinion, it wasn't really operating because it was not possible to reach Sarajevo and also because the Serb representatives walked out of the assembly as a group and out of the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is a well-known fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that that is why you did not pay attention to this document.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. In view of the composition of the government at the time, it could not be respected throughout the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And, anyway, the document was passed without any legal grounds. Vitezit was never declared a public corporation. It was not an enterprise that the government could appoint the managers of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the significance of the military industry, perhaps that's what prompted such a decision.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Probably because already at the time, people started thinking about strategic goals, and the military industry in Vitez was the most important segment, producing fuels, explosives, and missile fuels, and without those fuels, you cannot use any weapons; and, of course, all sides wanted to gain control of this factory, including, therefore, the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or I prefer not to call it the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina but, rather, the Muslim government.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the other military facilities within Bosnia-Herzegovina, Bugojno, Konjic, Novi Travnik, Gorazde, Pobjeda, Bratstvo, who controlled those factories?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: They were all in the territory controlled at the time by the BH army; that is, under the control of the Muslims, and they just lacked the Vitez factory to complete the chain, the technological chain, to be able to produce all the weaponry, and that is why they had aspirations towards it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you consider Vitez to be of particular significance for the BH army because of this strategically important factory?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: That is quite evident. There can be no question that it was an extremely important locality strategically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us now go on to the agreement reached between the HVO and the BH army. Tell us, are you aware of any agreement between the BH army and the HVO having to do with a distribution of these military products manufactured in those factories?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Since the beginning of the Serb aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina, because there were certain problems over the delivery of military equipment and distribution to users, we asked this question to be settled and that the official authorities let us know how these deliveries could be made, and this request resulted in an agreement, and the HVO and the TO at the time agreed that the resources should be divided up 50-50: 50 per cent to the HVO and 50 per cent to the TO. That is how we operated throughout '92 and a part of '93, because all of us at the time felt we were defending ourselves against the Serbs, and we were thus equipping ourselves to thwart the aggression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this agreement was reached in '92.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in '92.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long was it observed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: It was observed until the outbreak of the conflict between the Croats and the Muslims, that is, until April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you claim that all three factories delivered a half of their products to each side?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: All the military products manufactured in the three factories, SPS, Vitezit, and Sintevit, were divided up 50-50 per cent between the TO and the HVO throughout '92 until April 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether civilian authorities were familiar with this agreement?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly. We had to get approval from the civilian authorities for most of those deliveries, and there are documents showing the civilian authorities giving permission for passage of these products through areas where the BH army logistics centres were, which was formerly the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please now look at a specification of orders to all three factories?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D55/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us what this table shows?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: This table, as far as I can see, was compiled after the war between the Croats and the Muslims, and it has to do with claims for products delivered in '92 and '93 for the needs of the BH army, and this gives the number of the bill, the delivery papers, the invoices, and we can see from this that in the course of 1992 and '93, we delivered to the BH army special purpose products to the value of 2.911.587,20 German marks which, of course, we never collected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these are outstanding claims of the factory from the BH army.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: A similar such list or specification of claims exists for the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So neither the HVO nor the BH army paid anything?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no one paid anything, to my sorrow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Linked to this list, would you please look at these tables showing the kind of products involved, those that you call special purpose products?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at this specification of claims. In the first column, we have the number of the invoice, then we see that there are invoices dating back to '93, the amount and, lastly, notes indicating the places where those products were delivered. There is mostly Lukovac, Tuzla, and Visoko are mentioned, and Bugojno. What was situated in those places?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The logistics centre of the BH army. That is why they were delivered there. But afterwards, they were distributed throughout the area controlled by the TO, later the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you please now look at the new table where an indication is given of the kinds of products involved?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: This second table specifies the products distributed to various logistics centres, and you can see what was delivered: bullets, 152, with fuse, without fuse, warhead casings, the total number of bullets and so on. So, you see, there are about ten different products that we manufactured, and we distributed among logistics centres of the BH army and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the second table, it is clear that some products were sent to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I already said that it was 50-50 between the two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us, please, have you seen these documents before, these two documents, and do you know who issued them?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I did see these two documents before, because on the basis these documents after the war we tried to compensate the factories for the product delivered, but we didn't succeed. They were compiled by the administrative service of the SPS, because it was the last in the chain. So we can see from this table that in addition to the social enterprise Vitezit, the company Bratstva from Novi Travnik participated, because they manufactured casings and some other products, so that Bratstva from Novi Travnik participated in the manufacture of some of these products.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these military products that were delivered were registered, and after the war you made such tables in order to submit your claims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, by groups of products, and these were regularly signed by the person who took over the products to whom they were delivered, the logistics centre that they were delivered to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I have another 15 minutes perhaps, but not more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We will now take a break, a 30-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's continue where we left off. So how were these goods dispatched?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In vehicles -- in vehicles of the recipient, the person who received the goods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any permits requested for the passage of such vehicles?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Generally, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Defence document D50/2? Could you tell us, Mr. Divkovic, whether this is a permit for the passage of persons and goods?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a regular permit for movement of persons and goods. This is the dispatch of goods for Visoko. The names of the persons are here who are escorting the goods, and this was signed by the President of the HVO municipality of Vitez, Ivan Santic. You can see the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, and I think as far as I can see, it's also signed by Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is a permit for the SPS to transport goods to Visoko?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a permit for the SPS, that it can deliver the goods or load these goods onto a vehicle which arrived from Visoko, and the names of the drivers are here and the person who received the goods. So based on such a permit, the indicated goods were loaded and shipped. You can see from this that both the civilian and the military authorities agreed for these goods to be delivered to the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's also stated here that the persons, Omer Begic, Ramiz Smajic and Emir Kadic are escorting this vehicle. They're all from Visoko?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the names, are these Croats or Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: These are all Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the type of goods in the vehicles are shells and casings?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says, 105-millimetre shell cases, 120-millimetre mortars, and these are the goods according to the bill of lading numbers which are stated below.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these are these military goods that you spoke about that were delivered from the SPS?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have one more question regarding these shipments. You can see from these tables that you provided us with, that you gave to me, it can be seen from these tables that these are basically the calculations and the specifications that were compiled by the SPS company?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that you also carried out these sales and also the final processing of the data concerning the debt to the SPS company?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: From these tables that we looked at before, you can see that there are several components produced by different companies that are all part of the goods, but the final analysis was made by the SPS, and they also processed the data and they shipped these goods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please look at another bill of lading? Would the usher please --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D57/2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is also a shipment from SPS; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 446/92. This is also the same situation. The recipient is the logistics centre of the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Visoko, the purchaser is the one who is shipping the goods. These special purpose goods are being shipped, and these are shells filled with explosives in this case.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen such bills of lading before in the course of your work in Vitezit?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Such documents were issued every day, because products were shipped every day, so there's a whole pile of such documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Regarding this shipment of goods, I will show you an invoice from the 14th of December, '92, so would you please tell us whether such documents were usually issued, and could you please tell us if you're familiar with the contents of that document?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D58/2.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: This is a usual kind of document for all shipped goods. Invoices were issued in order to maintain records on all the deliveries that we made. So this is one of many such documents which were issued. You can clearly see whom it was issued to, and there are also bills of lading with signatures of the people who received the goods and indications of which logistics centre received the goods. You can see that this all went through the Visoko logistics centre. This is for the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. You can also see the dispatch note, you can see what was shipped, lead on -- yes. The goods were shipped to Olovo, the town of Olovo. To Visoko, Olovo, Olovo, Olovo. So these are mostly deliveries to Olovo where also there was a logistics centre of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the recipients, according to the dispatch notes were?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The buyers were the armed forces of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So invoices such as this one with dispatch notes were issued to the buyers?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were regularly issued to the buyers in order to maintain our financial records that we're obliged to do as any normal company is obliged. Also, one of the documents stated here also says that a permit was issued by the commander of the HVO Operative Zone. So you can see there was normal co-operation between the HVO and the BH army regarding the provision and preparations for defence against Serb aggression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the date on that document? So the date on that document is the 14th of December, 1992. So this is already quite close to the time of the conflict between Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We delivered our products normally in the course of '93 as well, until shortly before the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would also like to ask you about the names of the persons that are on certain dispatch notes, the persons that received the goods such as Rahman Merdic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Rahman Merdic was the deputy general manager of the SPS, and he issued the orders for delivery and he's a Muslim by nationality. Taken over by Fadil Karicic. He was a member of the armed forces of the B and H from Olovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he's also a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he's a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these documents would accompany every shipment, and based on these documents the tables were compiled that you brought to us?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These are original documents on the basis of which we compiled the charts that I brought. The dispatch notes are original documents indicating who received the goods and which goods were delivered, the quantity and all the other characteristics, so that we would have the exact information on each shipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So such invoices were sent to the HVO?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We sent invoices to the HVO and the BH army, including these specifications and other information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This invoice was issued to the amount of 39.984 German Marks, and it states on the invoice that payment date is the 29th of December of '92.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The usual term is 15 days from the invoice date, but the payment was not carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So regardless of the fact that the invoices were not paid, you regularly carried out the deliveries?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't really important whether the invoices were paid. What was important is that the goods were delivered and that we're all able to prepare ourselves for defence at that time exclusively from the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any time receive orders to stop deliveries of material to the Muslim side, meaning to the armed forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I never received such an order. I don't know if anybody amongst my colleagues received such an order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And according to your information, deliveries continued until the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Deliveries went on until April '94 -- excuse me, '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you please also tell us if you know who controlled or monitored the equal distribution of these special purpose goods? Was there some kind of control at the level of the factory, or at the level of the municipality or it's a military level?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Through the permits that we received from the Operative Zone control was also carried out. There was monitoring. So there were people who were responsible for this division. There was Mr. Franjo Sliskovic from the HVO Operative Zone, and Mr. Muhamed Nemes from the BH army Operative Zone. So they coordinated this information on the shipment of goods from the factories. So there were no misunderstandings in this matter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these are representatives of the logistics?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were representatives for logistics of the HVO and the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The 15th of April, 1993, would you please tell us what happened at the company on that day?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In my company, Vitezit, there was a meeting of the management personnel from 9.00 to 1.00 p.m., and we were discussing the usual problems regarding production, insurance, outstanding claims, securing funds for salaries, current problems that we encountered in our normal course of work. Others also were in the same situation. We were dealing with current problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't have any information about any actions that were being prepared on the part of the Croats or on the part of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was a very uncertain time, and there were incidents happening, so we had gotten used to these small incidents that were taking place. We looked at them as out of the ordinary events and we did not attach any particular significance to that, but there was nothing in particular, based on which we could conclude that something special was being prepared. So there was no indication of anything -- that anything was about to happen, because at that time we were getting -- we were getting ready to deliver food to our employees. So about ten tonnes of various goods were being loaded in trucks in Split, and we were expecting the arrival of those trucks. There were about 20 drivers. Out of those 20 drivers there were 9 Muslims who happened to be in Split in Croatia. The other SPS factories, the assistant general manager and the commercial affairs director, also the foreman of the plant for missile fuel, were all part of the delegation which went to Zagreb to discuss the supply with certain raw materials in order to continue production. So the breakout of the conflict, at that time they happened to be in Zagreb. So we couldn't really -- there was no way of assuming that anything would have happened. If this was so, these people would not have agreed to travel to Zagreb and we wouldn't have agreed for them to travel either. So once the conflict broke out, I must say that we did everything we could for those people who happened to be on their business trip in Zagreb and for the drivers to be safe and for them to stay there until it was safe for them to return to their places of residence. We had those people kept in hotels, they were secure, and when circumstances allowed, they all came back to their homes, and they were alive and well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people that you said, the 20 drivers who went to get the food from Split, you said this was 200 tonnes of food; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you manage to bring this food in later?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately not. All of this remained there, and then due to the circumstances there later, it wasn't possible to bring this shipment in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that the people who went to pick up this food, nine of them were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any of their names?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have some of the names. I don't have all of them. For example, Nesib Ahmic, Sulejman Ahmic, Muharem Dzidic, Ibrahim Cejvan, Nasif Sivro, Kasim Zlotrg, Izet Kalco, and a couple of others that I can't remember their names because it was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you managed to secure that they stay in Split because they couldn't return to Vitez; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We kept some of them for 15 days, some for 20 days, some even for a month until it was possible to bring them back safely to where they wanted to go, and we managed to do this. So these people were safe. There were no incidents, nothing unpleasant happened, and then they were returned to their homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether there was any watch organised at SPS during the night?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course, particularly with this kind of production, it was important to have a good guard or watch service, so this is also the case in SPS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this guard, in the night between the 15th and the 16th, on regular duty or were there any extraordinary measures taken?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: No extraordinary measures were taken. We had regular guard duty, and they rotated in shifts, so the shift that was on duty that day to be on watch carried out its duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people were in one shift?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: From 16 to 17 people were in one shift. On that day, on the night between the 15th and 16th of April, there were 15 persons in the shift. Out of those 16 people, there were eight Muslims: Alija Zukan, he was the chief of the shift, supervisor of the shift; Halim Dzalilovic was a guard; Salih Causevic, guard; Hamdija Spahic, guard; Salih Tosovic, guard; Izet Haskic, on fire duty and driver; Sedzad Hruskic on fire duty; and Midhat Foric, guard. So more than half of them were Muslims on that shift which was on duty in the company on the night between the 15th and the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these names that you stated, these are Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, these were Muslims who were in that shift, out of a total of 16 persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So any kind of raid in the company, maybe shelling the company or attempts to hit a warehouse, what consequences for Vitez would there be if this happened in view of the kind of goods that were being kept there?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it depends on which facility would be in danger. We had explosives warehouses that had maybe 500 tonnes of explosives there, and for those familiar with what explosives are, if this was ignited, it would pose a great danger in Vitez and it would create an ecological catastrophe, so we really took measures to make sure that something like that did not happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the guards prevented any such act of sabotage or provocation that may have occurred?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. There were guards on duty there to prevent any such event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When there was a threat of shelling of Vitez from Zenica, was that a threat that could have caused the destruction of Vitez and the surroundings?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Anyone who would hit the explosives depot would simply destroy the Lasva Valley. That's quite clear to anyone who has any even very superficial knowledge about explosives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was a very serious threat?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: It was a terrible threat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Divkovic. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel Radovic? Cross-examined by Mr. Radovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I only have one question which you may or may not be able to answer. Within the system of the factory, was there a record kept of the arrival of workers to work?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in every single department, there were such records.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there some kind of a list?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course. There were books in each department, so every foreman or leader of the shift had a list of the employees who were due to come to work, and we kept a record of the hours spent at work, and on the basis of those hours, the workers were paid.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. I assume you are going to tender those documents into evidence. No objection? All right. So it's from D53/2 up to D58/2. Yes. Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Any cross-examination by other Defence counsel? There is none -- Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: No one else has asked to cross-examine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Terrier? Mr. Blaxill?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. With your leave, I shall be cross-examining this witness. Good morning, Defence counsel, and good morning to you, sir. Cross-examined by Mr. Blaxill:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do have a few questions for you arising from your evidence. You were, I believe, the general manager of the Vitezit company; that is correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have described the composition of the staff, and particularly the management, as one that was very ethnically balanced; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed, if I understand you correctly, it seems that the philosophy was to make a positive effort to maintain the ethnic balance in the factory to reflect that of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the philosophy, as I said, in the system that prevailed before '91 and it was preserved after that as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you say that in management terms, the staffing remained pretty much the same right up to April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Not just the management but the entire personnel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say, though, that rotational layoffs of staff had to take place because of production difficulties after what you called the Serb aggression; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those layoffs also tailored to try and keep still the same sort of ethnic balance within the factory?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mostly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in a senior management position, sir, would you have dealings directly with your customers?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: With the workers, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, with the customers of the business, those who purchased the munitions from the factories.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Not too frequently. I had a commercial department, and that was their immediate responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who essentially were the customer contacts? Were they the local municipal authorities or were they national government who purchased from you as a factory?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The buyers during wartime, from the beginning of the Serb aggression on, these military goods were purchased by the HVO. They didn't really buy them, they just took them because they didn't pay for them, and the TO, which later was the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So by that, sir, do you mean that the military forces themselves did the purchasing, or did they do so through a civilian administration, like a Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The Defence Ministry at that time was not functioning at the level of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and there were two components of the armed forces: the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, which started out as the Territorial Defence, and the HVO, and they took these military products for the needs of their armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true, sir, that during the course of 1992, the HVO, as an institution, was both military and civilian in its nature?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: The HVO was a civilian institution, and it probably had a certain military component to it. The HVO was the civilian authorities, and the operation zone was the military component.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was the operation zone that you obviously were supplying with arms and munitions?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That can be seen from these permits and all the documents, who received the goods. He was the head of logistics of the operation zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I believe that the -- let us say the influence of the HVO increased considerably during 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: In what way?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not true that that effectively, by the end of 1992, became the governmental power in the region of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: No. As far as the factory is concerned, no. I said that the factory was immune to the policies pursued by political bodies, and our condition at the beginning was that the ruling parties and their military components should come to an agreement as to the way in which they would cooperate with the factory. Our aim being to avoid any confrontation or disputes among the managers of the factory and thereby prevent production and normal operations. Therefore, I repeat, no civilian authority of the HVO had any direct influence over the factory, and that is obvious from the composition of the management that was operating in the factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whilst you tried to divorce your factory and its management from the politics going on around you, is it not true you would be aware of what was happening in the area?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what exactly you mean "aware." Obviously the situation was not normal because there was a war. We were waging a war against the Serbs. We were a country that was the object of aggression. Obviously, the situation wasn't quite normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed. In order to avoid problems within your factory, you clearly must have known what you were trying to avoid so you'd be aware of what was going on outside.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: We just wanted to be able to concentrate on production, to take care of the workers employed in the factory, and that is why we required that the authorities agree as to what they wanted and then, when they conveyed to us those joint positions, we would implement them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were then aware of, say, the creation of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna? You were aware of its existence, were you, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that's a superfluous question. Of course, I was aware that the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was formed. But, but, I --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you were aware, were you not, that that entity had expressed itself as setting up a social, economic, cultural, territorial, and military entity for Croats within that part of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: No, that is not how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that you then carried on supplying to the Bosnian army, if I may use that expression, and to the HVO, in equal shares right through, you say, until April 1993?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at it, sir, you received, it seems, a very specific directive from the elected government in Sarajevo in November '92 which you saw fit to ignore. Why would you ignore such a directive of the national government?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't ignore the directive. If you looked carefully at the document, the directive was addressed to the provisional manager who was supposed to implement it. It was not up to me to implement it anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would refresh your memory, sir, that you referred to this as being a temporary management board in which, by the number 2, appears your name; below that of Dragan Nakic. You looked at this document earlier this morning, sir. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document I am referring to -- maybe we could put it back to the witness, if you would be so kind? I don't recall the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's D54/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I am obliged to you, sir. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you see before you a decision appointing a temporary managing board for the Vitezit company; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand correctly, sir, you told this Court this morning that you and the other members of the board refused to implement that central government decision; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: You misunderstood. This decision on appointing a temporary managing board and a temporary manager of the public corporation Vitezit is giving an instruction to the man appointed as the temporary manager to implement it. I said that this man, whose name is Nusret Kalco, who was appointed temporary manager, came to see me and said that he had no idea about this decision and that he believed that this decision could not be implemented.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was a decision of another. Very well. If we may move on, please, sir? I do recall you, however, referring at the time that you gave evidence on that document, that you referred to the government in Sarajevo as a "Muslim government." Is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think you said in this court that you believed that that government had lost credibility because the Serb members had walked out.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Not only the Serb members but also the Croatian because they couldn't attend government meetings because of the siege of Sarajevo, and that is why I said because of the composition of the members attending the meeting, because the people taking such decisions were Muslims. This decision should have been signed by the Prime Minister, Mr. Jure Pelivan, and not by the vice premier, Mr. Hakija Jurajlic, and Mr. Jure Pelivan never heard about this decision as he told me during a conversation that we had subsequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have there ever been instances in your commercial life, sir, where a deputy, to somebody else, has the authority to sign for that person in his absence?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: But this cannot be a permanent solution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you chose to take a certain view of the actions of a government by saying that you felt the wrong person had signed it because the vice-president had and not the president. Very well, sir. Now, in the area of Vitez in late 1992, what do you feel was the, if you like, the dominant governmental and military power in the area at that time?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I do not have sufficient information about the domination of the local government. For me it was important who had been elected at the 1991 elections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I noticed a little earlier, sir, when two documents were put to you regarding deliveries to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that they were dated no later than December of 1992. Now, is it not true that you ceased any supply to the BiH army earlier than the April '93 you've previously indicated?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: No. According to the information at my disposal that is not right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. It's just unfortunate then, sir, is it, that the examples we have pre-date 1993? Mr. Divkovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I really think that my learned colleague has no need to comment on the answers of this witness. He may ask him questions, listen to his answers and go on. I think such comments are inappropriate and unnecessary. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaxill, could you please refrain from commenting?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honours. I guess my interpretation of the realms of cross-examination are somewhat different to those of my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. She was right, Mr. Blaxill.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour, sir. I stand corrected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say that you had very strict requirements in respect of the completion of documents for the shipment of goods and supplies from your factories?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Documents were regularly filled in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be -- or was it the requirement that all details to be inserted on a document should be inserted, there would be no gaps?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, according to our approach and our rules, there should be no gaps because these are very sensitive products.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, sir. That's a point. I noticed -- if we have document D57/2, please. Mr. Divkovic, it may be my ignorance or a problem reading a translation, but it would appear that the document is lacking certain details such as quantities, the value of the shipment, the contract or order number, the registration number of the shipping vehicle, the number of cases being shipped, who took delivery. In other words, this would appear to be missing a lot of details. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that some details are lacking but this would be an exception. We could give you hundreds of other documents that are quite fully filled in. I don't know why this occurred, though this is just a bill of lading. The invoice would have to contain all the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So this is, you say, the buyer's copy of a bill of lading, and it is missing a lot of important detail, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it also a fact that from this document it's not really possible to show that these goods were shipped, would you agree, on the face of it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: I said that this document is faulty, but perhaps it would be the only one among a host of documents. This is not a large quantity, but you can see that the goods were shipped by Alija Zukan, and if that is of any importance, he's an individual who is a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I make no comment. Sir, if I could turn to D58/2, please. Could that be put? Now, again, Mr. Divkovic, just looking quickly through these documents, there would seem to be, in the majority of cases, some things again lacking on the face of the paperwork, particularly the number plates of vehicles, dates of dispatch. Again, they seem to be missing from the record-keeping.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: There are dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I -- again, I'm dealing from a translation copy, sir, so I hope we're not at cross-purposes. Does it in the first, say, six or seven sheets, we have a kind of table, and on my translation copies --

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Are we talking about the same document?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I sincerely hope, but we could compare just in case because I'm working from translations. Could the usher perhaps -- the ones I have is marked D58/2. In fact, the translations reads like that. Would it be that set? Sorry if we've marked the wrong -- I have a feeling that the problem is that the tabular format of the translation is not the same as the originals, which places me in some difficulty as I cannot read the originals to locate that. I think it's not such a significant point that I will take much more of the court's time on that. Thank you, Your Honours. Sorry, sir, we will not pursue that matter further. A list has been produced indicating the amount of supply of arms to the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that correct? You would recognise that document, sir? Yeah.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is -- just for absolute clarity, this purely applies to that force, there is nothing in reference to the HVO here?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. An identical specification was prepared and sent to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the only one that is produced in court today is that relating to the army of BiH; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but we can prepare another one if necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated, sir, that you considered your factories of strategic importance for the ABiH. That is right, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be true to say the same goes for the HVO?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that towards the end of 1992 the HVO actually provided guards for the factory to protect it -- or to protect them, I should say.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Not at the end of 1992. It could have been at the beginning of 1993 that several policemen were posted on the main entrance because of looting incidents and all other things that were happening in those days in the area where the factory was and where we were living.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was there any particular additional supply of arms to the ABiH out of the -- is it the Sintevit factory, the one with the predominantly Muslim management?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: There couldn't have been, because they were not the manufacturer of finished products.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So really, finished products had to go out via the SPS factory, is that correct, sir, or through Vitezit?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware -- this is, in fact, I believe, Prosecution Exhibit number 323. I wonder if that could be shown to the witness for a moment. I've been told 343. I apologise for that. I ask your indulgence for a moment, Your Honours, we have a slight housekeeping difficulty over the number of the document. I'll be just a moment. This apparently, although it appears as if it's a document that may have already gone into evidence it is not one. I have a fact I wish to refer to. I will make reference to that fact. The witness can confirm knowledge or not, and the document hasn't been served on the Defence so it will not be placed before him. I trust there's no objection to that, Your Honours. Mr. Divkovic, I'm sorry, you've been confused, you've been handed a wrong document. It doesn't matter. I just want to ask you about one fact about whether you are aware of this at all, sir, and are you aware that the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, their HVO main staff, issued some form of order in January 1993 stating that the HVO would be in complete military command and that all HVO and BH army units should submit to the command of the HVO? Were you aware of such an event, sir?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't aware.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I just have a couple more things at this time, but it will be just a few minutes. We're at five past twelve, Your Honour. Do you wish to take the break now? I'm probably like my learned friend was earlier, say, 15 to 20 minutes maximum to finish. You might like to take your break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We'll go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: We'll go on, sir? All right. Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the movement of vehicles in and out of the Vitez area carrying munitions, was that, in fact, arranged by or granted by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Generally, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, one other thing you earlier said, I believe, that the HVO, from time to time, would simply take what they wanted and, you know, hence you received no payment whether it was ordered or taken. Is that still correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: This is not correct. I didn't say that. I said we delivered goods to the BH army and to the HVO but neither of them paid for these goods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see, sir. Yes. Thank you. If I may ask, how were you able to maintain supplies of raw materials since the receiving forces were not paying for their munitions?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't have the ability to get new raw materials. The factories that supplied us before the conflict with the Serbs remained in the territory of Yugoslavia, and in Eastern Bosnia, in Gorazde. So as you probably yourself know, there was an embargo on the import of raw materials that we used in our manufacture. So we were using the raw materials that were there at the time in our factory. That is why we had the problem of operating at complete capacity. We were using the raw materials that were at the factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so did you have any particular request for increase of production during any part of 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: There was always that request to intensify production in accordance with our abilities, to use the existing capacities as much as possible, and also in view of the available raw materials.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But was there or was there no actual increase or did you just maximise at all times your resources?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: We used the resources that were available to us, because that was the only thing that we could do. So the intensity of production was not even close to the maximum production, but it was just on what was possible for us at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if armed forces of the BiH army, or the HVO or both were in a position to have an armed conflict in mid-April of 1993, they obviously had received those munitions over a period of time, sir; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. They received it from us for the whole time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'd just like to confer with my colleagues for a moment. There is just one small point I would like to confirm. Do you know, sir, an Ante Sliskovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that he was, in fact, someone who had to be a signatory for the dispatch of munitions from the factories?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would just like to tell my learned colleague, Mr. Blaxill, that the witness never mentioned the name of Ante Sliskovic, so I would prefer that the question not be asked in that way. If there is -- actually, the question here is about Franjo Sliskovic. Ante Sliskovic is a different person, and I think that this is not proper because the witness did not mention Ante Sliskovic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaxill, were you mentioning Ante Sliskovic or the other name?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the name I was endeavouring to reach is the person who was the, apparently, the major signatory for the dispatch of munitions from the factory. Now, perhaps I can rephrase that question, Your Honour, and suggest, firstly, was it a Mr. Sliskovic who was a major signatory for the dispatch of munitions from the factories?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DIVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Franjo Sliskovic, not Ante. He was mainly the person who would sign the dispatch documents for the goods shipped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. It was probably just a slip of the tongue on my part, Your Honour, nothing significant in it. Thank you, and I have no further questions.
